name: Bag of Empty Ooze Containers
summary: In Ironforge, Laris Geardawdle supplies empty jars for his study of Azeroth’s oozes. He means them to hold clean slime gathered in the wild.

sections.title: Field Research Equipment
sections.body: Laris Geardawdle studies the strange biology of Azeroth’s oozes. He found that they quickly take on the corruption around them, including Felwood’s tainted residues. So he commissioned sturdy jars that can hold acidic specimens without harming them. The bag carries enough jars to gather clean slime in wild regions, especially Un’Goro Crater, where ancient glutinous oozes live free of demonic taint.

faq.q: What is inside the Bag of Empty Ooze Containers?
faq.answer: The bag holds ten Empty Pure Sample Jars. Their glass can hold caustic ooze without damaging or contaminating a sample.

aliases: who gives bag of empty ooze containers
faq.answer: Laris Geardawdle, a gnome researcher in Ironforge’s Hall of Explorers, supplied the containers. He studies how slimes adapt to their surroundings.

faq.q: What kind of oozes are these jars meant to collect?
aliases: what slime goes in the jars
faq.answer: The jars are meant for pure, uncorrupted ooze. You can gather pristine slime from Un’Goro Crater’s glutinous oozes, unlike the blighted specimens in Felwood.

faq.q: Why does Laris need pure ooze samples?
faq.answer: Laris needs pure ooze to study how oozes absorb qualities from their surroundings. He can compare an uncorrupted specimen with polluted slimes from blighted regions.

angles.text: As a gnome, you can see the ingenuity in these durable, chemical-resistant jars. They let researchers carry dangerous, corrosive wildlife samples safely.
As an Alliance adventurer, you can help Laris Geardawdle with his ecological research in Ironforge. Bring him field samples from untamed places like Un’Goro Crater.
